taskTitle: Twelve HTTP status codes, by the book

checks.detail: a 8-step plan, read from the schema reply
2 phases had the tools designed for them

finalText:
I used RFC 9110, "HTTP Semantics" (June 2022), at https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9110.html. It is the current HTTP Semantics specification. A search turned up nothing that replaces it, but the rfc-editor.org info page returned a 404, so I couldn't check its "obsoleted by" field directly.

Section 15.1 of that page lists the heuristically cacheable codes as 200, 203, 204, 206, 300, 301, 308, 404, 405, 410, 414 and 501, and says all other codes are not heuristically cacheable. The sections for 203, 206, 308, 405, 410, 414 and 501 each say so too, and none of the other five sections do. The two sources therefore agree.

One wording difference: the 206 section says "unless otherwise indicated by explicit cache controls". The other sections say "unless otherwise indicated by the method definition or explicit cache controls". I still treated 206 as heuristically cacheable.

Two reason phrases changed from older RFCs: 413 is "Content Too Large" and 422 is "Unprocessable Content". Reason phrases are only recommendations in the spec (15.1).
